restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, Y4 is in the sub-class of 131,072 values of entry c66f230d's class, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 (2^-9.8132 of uniform word pairs; by Lemma F no counted success is lost) run the joint solver of Section 9.4, which returns every joint root, at most 128, and certifies each by recomputing its trial (Lemmas V and CV). Heuristic part: 2^59.461 aligned groups of 1,024 outer steps (2^69.461 outer steps, 2^90.461 walked trials) hold a trial whose other 128 chaining-value bits agree and that satisfies rule A, and the search finds it, with probability at least 0.39 under H1', H5' and H6'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, on a 16-register load/store machine where each fetch of a memory word costs one load. A group (random word, member, the step-CO lines not reading C0.d1, stored words) costs 333 units; each of its 1,024 outer steps (C0.d1 = s + r) costs 67 for omega, the first filter test and the loop, from a recount of the program's counted step CO and filter. All later work is prepaid from one credit counter K = 41,344 G = 2^74.797: 113 per first-test pass, 483 per passing outer step (full step CO), and the joint solver and certificate at 12,288 per outcome, 144 per node, 64 per leaf, 256 per root and 4,096 per passing step, at most 330,240. No sorting, no lookup by value, no table that grows with the trials. The run halts with failure only when the credits cannot pay a block or after the last group (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per group. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1', H5' and H6'. The factor 99,033,509,302 in H1' is 5/7 of the model's conditional count and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance of the same construction (counter 0, flags 11) because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. The filter is exact and needs no law of the words; there is no pass budget. The declared mean 38 of H6' rests on a participant validation of 2^24 outer steps, and the group ratio 13/2000 of H5' on scaled-down runs. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The groups, the credit counter, the joint solver and the certificate are defined in proof.md; the submitted program contains and counts the outer step and the filter.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test, the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value) and the seven tau values and eps of the filter are stored in the program (92 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces; beta* is the first of the 53 betas of the sub-class in an exhaustive ranking from the same counts, which also list its seven outcomes. preprocessing_log2 70 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 in full and is included in time_log2: the search alone is below 2^67.464 units, the selection below 2^69.976. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, selection and search, all held at once (sum below 2^44). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an ordinary outer step of proof.md 9.1 (eight independent uniform 32-bit words), let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials (t != 0, R = 0, rule A, and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter. Rate: E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = 99,033,509,302 * 2^-128, about 2^-91.473, where 99,033,509,302 = floor(5 * 138,646,913,024 / 7) is 5/7 of the conditional model count of Lemma S1 (a margin of 1.40). This is the first-moment part of the premise of entry e7b17fd1, restricted to the seven outcomes, which carry all of p; the dependence part of the earlier H1' is now H5prime-group-rho, and the id is kept for continuity. By Lemma PG (exact) an aligned group of 1,024 outer steps has 1024 E[N_o] listed good trials on average, and the run's G = 793,466,785,967,596,672 groups have at least Lambda = 1024 G (2^21 - 1) q = 0.4959080228891699 in all. By Lemma F (exact) every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter (Lemma S9), so the rate per member of Q* of a passing outer step is q / pi_o, about 2^-81.660 if pi_o equals the exact share pi.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values (Lemmas Q and Q2), E1.c1 in the cube Q* of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped. The statement is about ordinary outer steps; the search draws aligned groups of 1,024 outer steps that share six outer words and the member, and Lemma PG carries the first moment to them exactly. N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step; in a passing outer step the joint solver of Section 9.4 and step 3 certify exactly these trials (Lemmas V and CV).
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube does not bias the E3 side), taken at 5/7, the margin used by entries 6a600434 and 3f8e4e89 (GordoAR) and d598fe29 (winglock) on this track. The filter and the joint solver change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b) and CV). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1%; 2^43 real trials inside passing outer steps in which rule A, the stage-2 word share and the E1 test keep their values over all outer steps and the listed E1 outcome is 0.979 +- 0.022 of its value; a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted; and scaled-down runs of the counter arrangement at 8 and 10 bits with 6,933 and 2,132 complete successes against 6,948 and 2,112 expected. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 99,033,509,302 is assumed: 5/7 of the model count, a margin of 1.40 where the earlier entries of this participant used 2.00. The run is the shortest that gives the 0.39 floor under H1prime, H5prime and H6prime, so any shortfall of the rate below the assumed factor lowers the success bound below 0.39 (Section 10.4); with the count exact the run has 0.694 expected listed good trials. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S9) and partly assumed here, including how much success mass the dropped t = 0 member carries. Lemma F, Lemma S9 (a), Lemma PG and Lemmas V and CV use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter, no rule A and no sub-class.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an aligned group of proof.md 9.1 (1,024 outer steps with C0.d1 = s + r, r = 0..1023, s a uniform multiple of 1,024, the other six outer words and the member y shared), let N_g be the sum over its outer steps of N_o, the number of listed good valid trials over all of Q*. Dependence: E[N_g (N_g - 1)] <= (13/2000) E[N_g]. The groups of a run are independent and identically distributed, so with H1prime-rate-and-dependence and Lemma PG (means summing to at least Lambda = 0.4959080228891699), Lemma GB (exact: the indicator of z > 0 is at least z - z(z - 1)/2, and groups are independent) bounds the probability that no group of the run holds a listed good trial by exp(-(1 - 13/4000) Lambda) = 0.6099999999999999996631...; with the credit halt below exp(-1.7 * 10^11) (H6prime-total-work) the success bound is 0.3900000000000000003 > 0.39. The premise counts pairs inside one outer step and across outer steps of one group; a bound for single outer steps does not suffice, because the outer steps of a group share six words and the member (GPT Sol, answer AF 5.1). It replaces the dependence clause (ii) of the earlier H1prime.
heuristics.scope: The aligned groups of proof.md Section 9.1 with the counter construction of Section 8: the six constants, the sub-class of Y4, rule A, the cube of beta* and its seven E1 outcomes; all valid listed good trials (t != 0) of a group, whether or not their outer steps pass the filter (by Lemma F they all do).
heuristics.extrapolation: Scaled-down participant measurement (proof.md Section 13), untrusted by the harness. Reduction: 2-round BLAKE3 with W-bit words (W = 8 and 10), the IV cut to W bits, the BLAKE3 permutation, rotations (4,3,2,1) and (5,4,3,2), 2-bit toy bytes, messages of 7W - 1 and 7W + 7 toy bytes after t zero chunks, the last chunk compressed with flags 3 and counter t, t solved from the counter word as in step CT and t = 0 dropped, E1.d1 swept over the cube of the heaviest beta; every success is a match of all eight words, confirmed by complete hashing. W = 8: 6,933 successes (6,948 expected), no outer step with two. W = 10: 2,132 successes (2,112 expected), no outer step with two. Aligned groups of all 2^W values of X2 with the other six words and the member shared: 170.6 million groups at W = 8 and 50.1 million at W = 10, none with two successes. Pooling all members of a set into one group, a coarser grouping, gives at W = 10 one group with two among 2.82 million, a ratio of 2/2,132 = 0.00094 against the declared 0.0065, and none at W = 8. Partial events cluster inside an outer step, but the clustering exponent did not grow from W = 8 to W = 10. At 32 bits a group holds about 2^-60.47 listed good trials on average, so no direct measurement is possible; the declaration extrapolates the small toy ratios with a margin of about 7 over the pooled point estimate.
heuristics.limitations: Evidence, not proof. Only two widths. The toy varies X2 over its whole domain, where the search varies the low ten bits of C0.d1 with its high 22 bits and the member fixed; the toy constants, rotations, cube sizes and predicates differ from the 32-bit ones, and the toy has no rule A, no filter, no 17-bit member and no per-step cap. The Poisson upper limits quoted for the toy (0.00086 and 0.0028 within an outer step) are descriptive; distribution-free bounds with the trivial cap are vacuous; GPT Sol's three-width acceptance rule (upper limits at most 0.005 at three widths) is not met. Deterministically only the cap of Lemma S7 is known, which bounds a group's ratio by 3,145,727, useless here. If the count were exact, the 0.39 floor would hold up to a group ratio of 0.576 (Section 10.4).

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an ordinary outer step of proof.md 9.1, let Y_o be the credits the search takes for it when the run does not halt: 113 if the first test of the filter (the automaton of (2) on omega) passes, 483 more if the outer step passes, and X_o more, where X_o = 0 if it does not pass and otherwise X_o = 4,096 + 12,288 n_out + 144 n_node + 64 n_leaf + 256 n_root (searched outcomes, those rejected by their constants included; nodes taken from the stack, leaves included; leaves; joint roots of the joint solver of Section 9.4). Workload: E[Y_o] <= 38. Every outer step has Y_o <= 330,836 (Section 11). By Lemma PG the sum over an aligned group has mean at most 1024 * 38; with independent groups, Lemma WT (exact) bounds the probability that the run's credit budget K = 17 * 1024 G * 38 / 16 = 32,805,090,799,044,316,807,168 is spent before the run ends by exp(-G D(40.375/330,836, 38/330,836)) < exp(-1.7 * 10^11). The time bound charges K as a hard cap and does not depend on this premise. It replaces H4prime-pass-budget; the search has no pass, test-2, stage-2 or step-3 budget.
heuristics.scope: The search of proof.md Section 9.1 with the joint solver of 9.4 under GPT Sol's universal-table ledger (answer AI): 12,288 per searched outcome, 144 per node, 64 per leaf, 256 per root and 4,096 per passing outer step, plus 113 for the second test of the filter and 483 for the full step CO of a passing outer step. The mean is over all ordinary outer steps, not over passing ones, so it holds no separate premise on the pass share.
heuristics.extrapolation: Participant validation (proof.md Section 13), untrusted by the harness: the ledger, the seeds and the code hashes were frozen before sampling and unchanged after; 2^24 independent ordinary outer steps were drawn by 8 processes from fresh SHA-256-derived seeds, the size fixed in advance, no optional stopping, all pooled. Sum of Y_o 504,500,502, mean 30.0706 (sd 766.5), largest 148,980 against the cap 330,836; first-test passes 914,061, passing outer steps 18,787; events 23,566 outcomes, 173,929 nodes, 8,768 leaves and 0 roots; cross-checks against the program's step CT, the root counts and the per-guess bounds found no difference. The bounded-KL upper confidence bound for a variable in [0, 330,836] at error 10^-6 is 34.3017 (GPT Sol, answer AG 2.1; no variance or tail assumption). The rule fixed before the run, ceil(max(U, 1.25 * mean)) = ceil(37.588), gives the declared 38.
heuristics.limitations: The samples come from Python's MT19937 with fresh seeds, which stands in for independent uniform words and is not proved to be such. No outer step had a joint root, so the 256-per-root term never entered the sum and is covered only through the cap. The events are those of the participant's implementation, which builds a table per outcome with the same transition relation as the universal table, not a run of the Section 11 layout; the universal table and the credit counter have not been implemented. The confidence error 10^-6 is not subtracted from the success bound, because 38 is declared, not certified; the validation is external evidence, not part of the algorithm, and is not charged (charged by GPT Sol's conservative ledger it would leave time_log2 at 70.21). If the premise fails, the run may halt on its credits, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound.
